question.prompt: Let \(a\mathbin{@}b\) represent the operation on two numbers, \(a\) and \(b,\) which selects the larger of the two numbers, with \(a\mathbin{@}a=a.\) Let \(a\mathbin{!}b\) represent the operation which selects the smaller of the two numbers, with \(a\mathbin{!}a=a.\) Which of the following three rules is (are) correct? \[ \begin{aligned} (1)\quad&a\mathbin{@}b=b\mathbin{@}a,\\ (2)\quad&a\mathbin{@}(b\mathbin{@}c)=(a\mathbin{@}b)\mathbin{@}c,\\ (3)\quad&a\mathbin{!}(b\mathbin{@}c)\\ &\quad=(a\mathbin{!}b)\mathbin{@}(a\mathbin{!}c). \end{aligned} \]

solutions.explanation:
Each identity can be checked by identifying the value selected on each side.

Rule (1) holds because exchanging two numbers does not change their larger value. Rule (2) holds because each side selects the largest of \(a,b,c\): grouping two numbers first does not change that final selection. These statements also hold when some numbers are equal.

For rule (3), interchanging \(b\) and \(c\) leaves both sides unchanged, so suppose \(b\le c\). Then \(b\mathbin{@}c=c\), and the left side is \(a\mathbin{!}c\).

If \(a\le c\), then \(a\mathbin{!}c=a\), while \(a\mathbin{!}b\le a\). Thus the right side selects \(a\), agreeing with the left side.

If \(a\ge c\), then \(b\le c\le a\), so \(a\mathbin{!}b=b\) and \(a\mathbin{!}c=c\). The right side therefore selects \(c\), again agreeing with the left side. These cases include equality and cover every possibility.

All three rules are correct, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Apply the larger and smaller selection rules
